title: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties - Test 4

questions.q:
Given below are the two statements: one is labeled as Assertion (A) and the other is labeled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): There is a considerable increase in covalent radius from $N$ to $P$. However from $As$ to $Bi$ only a small increase in covalent radius is observed.

Reason (R): covalent and ionic radii in a particular oxidation state increases down the group.

In the light of the above statement, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.solution:
There is a considerable increase in covalent radius from $N$ to $P$. However, from $As$ to $Bi$ only a small increase in covalent radius is observed. This is due to the presence of completely filled d and/or f orbitals in heavier members.

As going down in a group, the number of shells increases, hence the covalent and ionic radii increases.

Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

But the correct explanation is the presence of completely filled d and f-orbitals of heavier members.

questions.q:
Bond dissociation energy of $E - H$ bond of the "${H}_{2}E$" hydrides of group $16$ elements (given below), follows order.
(A)~$O$
(B) $S$
(C) $Se$
(D) $Te$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.solution:
Bond strength is inversely proportional to the bond length of& $E - H$~bond of hydrides of 16th group hydrides. The bond length increases down the group. Hence, bond dissociation enthalpy decreases down the group.

Hence, bond dissociation energy of $E - H$ bond in hydrides of group 16 follows the order

${H}_{2}O > {H}_{2}S > {H}_{2}Se > {H}_{2}Te$.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements. One is labelled as
Assertion $A$ and the other is labelled as Reason $R$.
Assertion $A$ : The first ionization enthalpy for oxygen is lower than that of nitrogen.

Reason $R$~: The four electrons in $2p$ orbitals of oxygen experience more electron-electron repulsion.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both $A$~and $R$ are correct and $R$ is the correct explanation of $A$.
Both $A$ and $R$ are correct but $R$ is NOT the correct explanation of $A$.

$A$ is correct but $R$ is not correct.
&
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.solution:
Ionization energy of oxygen is less than that of nitrogen because& $2p$~subshell~of nitrogen is half filled, and half filled orbitals have some extra stability, so removing electrons from them will be little more difficult.
And In oxygen atom, $2$ of the $four2p$ electrons must occupy the same $2p$ orbital resulting in an increased electron electron-repulsion.

$N = 1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{3}$

$O = 1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{4}$

questions.q: The acidic, basic and amphoteric oxides, respectively, are
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.solution:
Non-metal oxides are acidic in nature as they produce acidic solution by reacting with water, so here& ${Cl}_{2}O, {P}_{4}{O}_{10}, {SO}_{3}$~are acidic oxides which produce~$HOCl, {H}_{3}{PO}_{4}, {H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$~respectively, with water.

Alkali metal and alkaline earth metal oxides are basic in nature, as~they produce metal hydroxide~solution with water and metal hydroxides are basic in nature.

Here,~${Na}_{2}O, CaO, {Li}_{2}O, MgO$~are basic hydroxides which form~$NaOH, Ca\left(OH\right)2, LiOH, Mg\left(OH\right)2$~respectively, with water.

${Al}_{2}{O}_{3}$ is amphoteric oxide as it can react either with acid or base to form salt and water.

questions.q:
Given two statements below :

Statement I : In ${Cl}_{2}$ molecule the covalent radius is double of the atomic radius of chlorine.

Statement II : Radius of anionic species is always greater than their parent atomic radius.

Choose the most appropriate answer from options given below&
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.solution:
In ${Cl}_{2}$ molecule, the covalent radius is half of the internuclear distance, so statement~ \left(I\right)$~is false. The covalent radius is little smaller than the actual radius of the atom~of chlorine due to overlapping during formation of covalent bond.

For the same element, anion has lower effective nuclear charge than atom~so, anion is larger than the parent atom. That means~statement \left(II\right)$& is correct.

questions.q: For elements $B, C, NLi, Be, OandF$, the correct order of first ionisation enthalpy is
options: $Li < Be < B < C < O < N < F$
$B < Li < Be < C < N < O < F$
$Li < Be < B < C < N < O < F$
$Li < B < Be < C < O < N < F$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.solution:
The first ionisation energy varies predictably across the periodic table.& As we move from left to right across a period, the ionisation energy of elements increases. This is due to the decrease in the size of atoms across a period. The valence electrons get closer to the nucleus of an atom as we move from left to right due to increased nuclear charge. The force of attraction between the nucleus and the electrons increases and hence more energy is required to remove an electron from the valence shell.& Ionisation energy of boron being unexpectedly less than that for beryllium due to the 2s orbital being totally filled in beryllium, whereas boron has one electron in a 2p orbital as well, and the 2s orbital is shielded much more than the 2p orbital. Ionisation energy& is more for nitrogen than oxygen because nitrogen is more stable due to its half-filled electronic configuration.

$Li < B < Be < C < O < N < F$

questions.solution:
A metal is a material that, when freshly prepared, polished, or fractured, shows a lustrous appearance, and conducts electricity and heat relatively well. Metals are typically malleable (they can be hammered into thin sheets) or ductile (can be drawn into wires)

On moving top to bottom of the periodic table metallic character increases and on moving left to right metallic character decreases.

Metallic character is directly& proportional to the atomic size.

The correct order of atomic size of the given elements is& $Na > Mg > Be > Si > P$.

Hence, correct order of metallic character is~$Na > Mg > Be > Si > P$

All these elements are form 3rd period except beryllium which is from second period

Na& is an alkali metal

Mg and Be& are& alkaline earth metals,&

Phosphorous belongs to a group which is commonly called as pnicogens.

Si belongs to 14th group

In the first transition series, the first and second ionization enthalpy values increase slowly on moving across the period. questions.q: The element having the highest first ionization enthalpy is
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.solution:
The first ionisation energy is the energy needed to remove the outermost, or highest energy, electron from a neutral atom in the gas phase.

The ionisation energy decreases from top to bottom in groups, and increases from left to right across a period. Nitrogen and carbon belong to second period elements, hence they have more ionisation energy than the other two elements.

It is highest for nitrogen because nitrogen is a more stable half-filled electronic configuration.

$Al < Si < C < N$; ${IE}_{1}$ order.

Hence option C is the answer.
